STAGE: independent scoring pass over four frozen candidate bundles.
GOAL: place the four proposals (SUCC-GEO-CBTAB, BFRQ-KARCHER-MASS, MIXCURV-FIBRE-RQ, poincare-frechet-successor-codebook) under rubric rank-2026-10-v1, grounding each placement in the shared evidence bundle only.
READ: scope contract, experiment policy, selection policy, the four proposals and the four evidence bundles (all bundles share E1-E13 with identical observed rows E4-E11).
OBSERVED (evidence): E5 shows strong directed-transition structure (top-1 successor mass 0.4375 vs 0.0543 across entropy quintiles, Spearman -0.973). E6/E7 show the frozen baselines: l1_br recall@10 0.04671, l1_br_euclid 0.06207, l1_only 0.06233, resample 0.06363, and the curved-successor decoding variants successor_geodesic_coarse 0.05500, successor_geodesic_coarse_v2 0.05463, tangent_successor_residual 0.05500, i.e. below the Euclidean baselines, with gold prefix survival collapsing at depth 3 (0.161 for l1_br_euclid). E8 gives the first-level capacity ceiling: pair share of 0.3106 at K=16 falling to 0.1547 at K=64 and 0.0822 at K=256. E11 shows the existing baseline SIDs have only 0.0907 same-first-prefix rate versus a 0.067 permuted null, so level-1 behavioural alignment is weak.
REASONING: (i) poincare-frechet-successor-codebook is the only arm whose behaviour weights and curved geometry enter the same connected path at assignment, weighted commitment (encoder gradient) and the Fréchet code estimator, with eta=1 so the step actually moves codes; its estimator stays anchored to assigned latents so reconstruction is not abandoned; its constants (clip [0.25,4], batch normalisation, self-transition removal) are documented defaults, and it directly targets the weak first-prefix alignment in E11 and the small-K grouping benefit in E8 without a separate margin loss. (ii) BFRQ-KARCHER-MASS is the same class of idea but weaker/safer: assignment is declared untouched while codes live in the ball, the weight w_i = 1+log1p(mu) is mild, and the Karcher step is damped by eta=1/(1+N_k), so it risks being near-inert (its own risk list admits the hyperbolic mean contracts and mu may be near-uniform). (iii) MIXCURV-FIBRE-RQ is genuinely new (per-item behaviour statistic as the mixing coordinate of a Poincare/sphere product) and changes both assignment and estimator, but its premise (hierarchy vs lateral prefix mixing) is not what the evidence localises: E7 shows level-1 NLL already 0.00 in l1_br while E6 shows the loss is at depth 3, and the spherical fibre adds an unconstrained rotational degree of freedom plus trainable-curvature interactions in a 72000-step single run. (iv) SUCC-GEO-CBTAB has the weakest specification: the SPEC text is deferred ("see SPEC EQUATIONS"), the triplet margin constant is not stated or derived, gradient flows only into codebooks with assignment untouched, and its risk list concedes both slow code relocation and collapse to duplicate codes; the E6 geodesic-successor variants at 0.055 are the closest observed precedent and they underperform.
OPEN: none; final ranking recorded in the next record.

STAGE: final answer, ranking of the four proposals under rank-2026-10-v1.
GOAL: emit the complete ranked verdict, one line per proposal, positions 1..4 with no ties or gaps.
EVIDENCE USED: E5 (transition structure), E6/E7 (baseline and geodesic-successor recall and per-position NLL), E8 (first-level capacity ceiling K=16 0.3106 -> K=256 0.0822), E11 (baseline same-first-prefix 0.0907 vs 0.067 null), plus each proposal's own specification, cost, safeguards and risk list.
ANSWER:
RANK: poincare-frechet-successor-codebook | position=1 | reason=Only arm where behaviour weights and Poincare geometry share one live path at assignment, weighted commitment and the Frechet code estimator with eta=1, so it can move SIDs; its weights are popularity-adjusted and clipped while its estimator stays anchored to assigned latents, targeting the weak first-prefix alignment in E11 (0.0907 vs 0.067 null) and the small-K grouping advantage in E8 without a separate margin loss.
RANK: BFRQ-KARCHER-MASS | position=2 | reason=Same curved-estimator family and its tau=median||z|| and p99 weights are measured, but assignment is left untouched while codes move into the ball, the weight 1+log1p(mu) is mild and the Karcher step is damped by 1/(1+N_k), so per its own risks (hyperbolic contraction, near-uniform mu) it can be computationally inert against the >0.065 target implied by the E6 ceiling of 0.06363.
RANK: MIXCURV-FIBRE-RQ | position=3 | reason=A real product-manifold coupling with a measured per-item clustering statistic, but the evidence does not localise the failure at level-1 hierarchy/lateral mixing (E7 gives T1 NLL 0.00 for l1_br while E6 shows collapse at depth 3, 0.161), and the spherical fibre plus trainable curvatures add an unconstrained rotational degree of freedom in a single 72000-step run.
RANK: SUCC-GEO-CBTAB | position=4 | reason=Weakest specification in the bundle (SPEC deferred to "see SPEC EQUATIONS", triplet margin constant neither stated nor derived) and codebook-only gradient with untouched assignment, while its own risk list concedes slow relocation and duplicate-code collapse; the nearest observed precedent, the E6 geodesic-successor variants at 0.05500/0.05463, sits below the 0.062-0.064 Euclidean baselines.
OPEN: none.
